segments.text: The Personal Protective Equipment, PPE, worn by actors in this video was
segments.zh: 本视频中演员所穿戴的个人防护装备（PPE），是

segments.text: selected based on a risk assessment of the chemicals used in the experiment
segments.zh: 根据对实验所用化学品

segments.text: and conditions simulated in the activity. In scenes where the presenter did not wear PPE
segments.zh: 以及活动中模拟的条件进行的风险评估来选择的。在主持人

segments.text: while in the lab, all chemicals were removed to eliminate chemical hazards.
segments.zh: 于实验室内未穿戴个人防护装备的镜头中，所有化学品都已移走，以消除化学危害。

segments.text: In this video, we'll go over various methods for dealing with lab emergencies.
segments.zh: 在本视频中，我们将介绍应对实验室紧急情况的各种方法。

segments.text: For this video, we'll assume you've already completed the first three steps of RAM.
segments.zh: 在本视频中，我们假设你已经完成了 RAMP 的前三步：

segments.text: Recognize hazards, assess risks, and minimize risks.
segments.zh: 识别危害、评估风险和最小化风险。

segments.text: Usually when things go wrong in the lab, either someone knew they were doing something unsafe
segments.zh: 通常，实验室里出问题的时候，要么是有人明知自己在做不安全的事

segments.text: and did it anyway, or someone didn't know that they were doing something unsafe.
segments.zh: 却还是做了，要么是有人不知道自己在做不安全的事。

segments.text: These are preventable situations if one follows the first three steps of RAM,
segments.zh: 如果遵循 RAMP 的前三步，这些情况都是可以预防的，

segments.text: but equipment failures or unexpected power outages can occur in any case.
segments.zh: 但设备故障或意外停电无论如何都可能发生。

segments.text: It is prudent to prepare for emergencies.
segments.zh: 为紧急情况做好准备是明智的。

segments.text: Labs are required to have emergency equipment available and must be inspected regularly
segments.zh: 实验室必须配备应急设备，并且必须由你所在的机构

segments.text: by your institution. Every time you enter a lab, take note of the location of emergency equipment.
segments.zh: 定期检查。每次进入实验室时，都要留意应急设备的位置。

segments.text: This is part of preparing for emergencies.
segments.zh: 这是为紧急情况做准备的一部分。

segments.text: Now let's look at four common lab emergencies and how to deal with them.
segments.zh: 现在我们来看四种常见的实验室紧急情况以及如何应对。

segments.text: Broken glass spills on people, spills in the lab, and fires.
segments.zh: 碎玻璃、溅到人身上的化学品、实验室中的洒漏，以及火灾。

segments.text: If any of these occur, be sure to notify your instructor immediately.
segments.zh: 如果发生其中任何一种情况，一定要立即通知你的老师。

segments.text: Although broken glass usually doesn't qualify as an emergency,
segments.zh: 虽然碎玻璃通常算不上紧急情况，

segments.text: it is a fairly common mishap in labs that require some attention.
segments.zh: 但它是实验室中相当常见、需要引起注意的意外。

segments.text: One obvious hazard is that broken glass has sharp edges.
segments.zh: 一个明显的危害是碎玻璃有锋利的边缘。

segments.text: If the broken glass is on the floor,
segments.zh: 如果碎玻璃在地板上，

segments.text: the first action is to isolate the area so that no one walks through the glass.
segments.zh: 首先要隔离该区域，以免有人踩过玻璃。

segments.text: Inform your instructor about the broken glass and they will help you deal with it.
segments.zh: 把碎玻璃的情况告诉老师，他们会帮你处理。

segments.text: Cleaning up broken glass is usually done with a brush and dust pan.
segments.zh: 清理碎玻璃通常用刷子和簸箕。

segments.text: To protect others, broken glass is discarded in a special container
segments.zh: 为了保护他人，碎玻璃要丢弃在专门的容器中，

segments.text: and never in a regular waste paper basket.
segments.zh: 绝不能丢进普通的废纸篓。

segments.text: Broken glass that is contaminated with a chemical deserves special treatment.
segments.zh: 沾有化学品的碎玻璃需要特殊处理。

segments.text: Inform your instructor about any such situation.
segments.zh: 遇到这种情况，要告诉老师。

segments.text: What should you do if you're exposed to a hazardous chemical as the result of a spill?
segments.zh: 如果因为洒漏而接触到有害化学品，你该怎么办？

segments.text: You should always be wearing eye protection,
segments.zh: 你应该始终佩戴眼部防护用品，

segments.text: but if a chemical does get in your eyes, use the eyewash station to flush it out.
segments.zh: 但如果化学品真的进入眼睛，要使用洗眼器把它冲洗出来。

segments.text: Be sure to rinse for at least 15 minutes or longer.
segments.zh: 一定要冲洗至少 15 分钟或更长时间。

segments.text: This may seem like a long time,
segments.zh: 这可能看起来时间很长，

segments.text: but it can take a while to flush out the chemicals
segments.zh: 但要冲洗掉可能已被眼部组织吸收的化学品

segments.text: that may have absorbed into the tissues of your eye.
segments.zh: 需要一段时间。

segments.text: Your instructor will assist you in seeking medical attention.
segments.zh: 老师会协助你就医。

segments.text: If a liquid spills on your hand or lower arm,
segments.zh: 如果液体洒到你的手上或小臂上，

segments.text: go to a sink and flush the area with lots of water.
segments.zh: 要到水槽边用大量的水冲洗该部位。

segments.text: If you're wearing a long sleeve shirt, it's best to remove the shirt
segments.zh: 如果你穿的是长袖衬衫，最好把衬衫脱掉，

segments.text: or you can cut off the sleeve to remove any chemical that's soaked into the fabric.
segments.zh: 或者把袖子剪掉，以去除渗入衣料中的化学品。

segments.text: If the chemical can't be washed off at the sink,
segments.zh: 如果在水槽边无法冲洗掉化学品，

segments.text: use a safety shower to flush the area with water.
segments.zh: 就用紧急喷淋装置用水冲洗该部位。

segments.text: You may need to remove any clothing that's been soaked with the chemical.
segments.zh: 你可能需要脱掉被化学品浸湿的衣服。

segments.text: And as I learned firsthand, the shower drops a lot of water all at once.
segments.zh: 正如我亲身体会到的，喷淋装置会一下子冲下大量的水。

segments.text: If you spill a dry chemical in your skin, we're just using baking soda here,
segments.zh: 如果你把干燥的化学品洒到皮肤上——我们这里用的只是小苏打——

segments.text: it's best to scrape off most of the chemical before rinsing with water.
segments.zh: 最好先把大部分化学品刮掉，再用水冲洗。

segments.text: A scupula, credit card, or student ID does this well.
segments.zh: 用药匙、信用卡或学生证都能很好地做到这一点。

segments.text: Be sure to clean them after use.
segments.zh: 用完后一定要把它们清洗干净。

segments.text: If liquid spills on the lab bench or on the floor,
segments.zh: 如果液体洒在实验台上或地板上，

segments.text: this can create a number of unsafe conditions including slipping on a wet floor.
segments.zh: 就可能造成许多不安全的状况，包括在湿地板上滑倒。

segments.text: In general, it's not your responsibility to clean up a spill of a liquid.
segments.zh: 一般来说，清理液体洒漏不是你的责任。

segments.text: Your instructor will take care of this using a spill kit.
segments.zh: 老师会用泄漏应急处理包来处理。

segments.text: However, you can do a few things to help.
segments.zh: 不过，你可以做几件事来帮忙。

segments.text: You should inform other students in the immediate area
segments.zh: 你应该通知附近区域的其他同学，

segments.text: and make sure you or someone else informs your instructor.
segments.zh: 并确保你或其他人通知老师。

segments.text: For a spill on a lab bench or floor,
segments.zh: 对于实验台或地板上的洒漏，

segments.text: you can remove items from the immediate area if it's safe to do so.
segments.zh: 如果安全的话，你可以把附近区域的物品移走。

segments.text: If you've been trained, you can isolate the spill
segments.zh: 如果你接受过培训，可以通过在洒漏物周围

segments.text: by pouring a ring of sand or absorbent around it.
segments.zh: 倒一圈沙子或吸附材料来隔离洒漏。

segments.text: Your instructor will decide if the lab needs to be evacuated.
segments.zh: 老师会决定实验室是否需要疏散。

segments.text: Fires in academic labs are not very common,
segments.zh: 教学实验室里的火灾并不常见，

segments.text: and when they occur, they tend to be small.
segments.zh: 而且即使发生，往往规模也很小。

segments.text: However, they will pose a significant risk.
segments.zh: 然而，它们会带来重大风险。

segments.text: It's best to take steps to prevent fires as well as be prepared to respond to them.
segments.zh: 最好既采取措施预防火灾，又做好应对火灾的准备。

segments.text: A good way to understand fire is to look at the fire triangle.
segments.zh: 理解火的一个好方法是看燃烧三角形。

segments.text: Three things are needed to start a fire.
segments.zh: 引发火灾需要三样东西：

segments.text: A substance that can burn, an oxidizing agent, and an ignition source.
segments.zh: 可燃物、氧化剂和点火源。

segments.text: Let's look at possible sources for each side of the triangle.
segments.zh: 我们来看看三角形每条边可能的来源。

segments.text: First, let's talk about fuel sources.
segments.zh: 首先，我们来谈谈燃料来源。

segments.text: Some chemicals can burn and some cannot.
segments.zh: 有些化学品能燃烧，有些不能。

segments.text: Read the label for every chemical you use to determine if it's flammable.
segments.zh: 阅读你使用的每种化学品的标签，以确定它是否易燃。

segments.text: The GHS pictogram on the bottle will also alert you to this hazard
segments.zh: 瓶子上的 GHS 象形图也会提醒你注意这种危害，

segments.text: and note how similar the pictograms are for flammable and oxidizer.
segments.zh: 注意易燃物和氧化剂的象形图有多么相似。

segments.text: Okay, what about an oxidizing agent?
segments.zh: 好，那氧化剂呢？

segments.text: Flammable compounds are oxidized when they burn,
segments.zh: 易燃化合物燃烧时会被氧化，

segments.text: and the most common oxidizing agent is all around us.
segments.zh: 而最常见的氧化剂就在我们周围。

segments.text: It's the oxygen in the air.
segments.zh: 那就是空气中的氧气。

segments.text: Finally, any ignition source will start the fire.
segments.zh: 最后，任何点火源都会引发火灾。

segments.text: This is usually a flame from a match or Bunsen burner or an electrical spark.
segments.zh: 通常是火柴或本生灯的火焰，或者电火花。

segments.text: Small, contained fires can be extinguished by simply
segments.zh: 小规模、受控的火只需

segments.text: placing a watch glass or large beaker over them.
segments.zh: 用一块表面皿或一个大烧杯盖住就能扑灭。

segments.text: This deprives a fire of oxygen.
segments.zh: 这样可以隔绝火的氧气。

segments.text: Removing any side of the fire triangle extinguishes the fire.
segments.zh: 去掉燃烧三角形的任何一条边，火就会熄灭。

segments.text: Larger fires will likely require the use of a fire extinguisher.
segments.zh: 较大的火可能需要使用灭火器。

segments.text: There are various types of fire extinguishers,
segments.zh: 灭火器有多种类型，

segments.text: but labs are generally equipped with the A, B, C type.
segments.zh: 但实验室一般配备 ABC 型灭火器。

segments.text: This will work on everything except active metal fires.
segments.zh: 它适用于除活泼金属火灾以外的所有火灾。

segments.text: Fire code requires that an appropriate extinguisher be located in all labs.
segments.zh: 消防规范要求所有实验室都配备合适的灭火器。

segments.text: When using any extinguisher, use the pass technique.
segments.zh: 使用任何灭火器时，都要采用 PASS 法：

segments.text: Pull a pin, aim at the base of the fire,
segments.zh: 拔出保险销，对准火焰根部，

segments.text: squeeze the handle, and sweep along the base of the fire.
segments.zh: 压下手柄，沿着火焰根部左右扫射。

segments.text: If there's a fire in your lab,
segments.zh: 如果你的实验室发生火灾，

segments.text: your instructor will probably be the one to use the extinguisher.
segments.zh: 很可能由老师来使用灭火器。

segments.text: You should know the pass technique in case you encounter a fire.
segments.zh: 你应该了解 PASS 法，以防遇到火灾。

segments.text: As with other emergencies, your instructor will tell you what to do in case of a fire
segments.zh: 和其他紧急情况一样，老师会告诉你发生火灾时该怎么做，

segments.text: and if you are expected to use a fire extinguisher.
segments.zh: 以及是否需要你使用灭火器。

segments.text: On rare occasions, something can happen that requires evacuation of the lab.
segments.zh: 在极少数情况下，可能会发生需要疏散实验室的情况。

segments.text: If it is safe to do so, turn off your electrical equipment and gas burner,
segments.zh: 如果安全的话，关掉你的电气设备和燃气灯，

segments.text: close the sash when working in a hood, and exit the lab.
segments.zh: 如果在通风柜中操作，要关上拉门，然后离开实验室。

segments.text: As you progress in your science education,
segments.zh: 随着你科学学习的深入，

segments.text: you will learn more about various kinds of lab hazards.
segments.zh: 你会更多地了解各种实验室危害。

segments.text: Preparing for emergencies requires forethought.
segments.zh: 为紧急情况做准备需要事先考虑。

segments.text: Responding effectively and safely requires training and practice.
segments.zh: 有效而安全地应对需要培训和练习。

segments.text: Many scientists can tell stories about lab mishaps.
segments.zh: 许多科学家都能讲出实验室意外的故事。

segments.text: Following the ramp steps will minimize harm to people and property.
segments.zh: 遵循 RAMP 的步骤可以把对人员和财产的伤害降到最低。

segments.text: To learn more about the other steps in ramp,
segments.zh: 想了解 RAMP 的其他步骤，

segments.text: be sure to check out the other five videos in this series.
segments.zh: 一定要看看本系列的其他五个视频。

segments.text: You can find them by clicking here,
segments.zh: 你可以点击这里、

segments.text: checking out the links in the description, or visiting acs.org slash safety videos.
segments.zh: 查看描述中的链接，或访问 acs.org/safetyvideos 找到它们。
